newsitem.title: UK: GDR REPORT - Indian GDRs slide with weak Bombay.
newsitem.headline: GDR REPORT - Indian GDRs slide with weak Bombay.

text.p: Indian global depositary receipts traded lower in London on Tuesday following sharp losses in Bombay, where trading resumed after a four-day weekend.
Sellers had the upper hand for most of the morning before some two-way business emerged later in the day, allowing shares to close just off the lows.
But dealers said the mood remained edgy following the biggest fall in the Bombay index in nearly five months, a loss of 155.60 to 4,165.37.
"The market is very nervous ahead with everybody trying to work out where the bottom is going to be," said one.

Among individual stocks, BSES was weak, falling 68 cents to $19.25/20.25, while ICICI came off recent highs, shedding 92 cents to $17.25/18.25. But Indian Hotels bucked the trend, adding 25 cents to $19.00/20.00.
The HSBC James Capel India GDR index lost 1.73 points, or 2.09 percent, to 81.18, a premium of 16.65 percent to the local market.
The Cazenove Indian GDR index, which measures changes from midday to midday, was down 1.40 points at 92.58.
Korean GDRs were also weaker as the local market took a hammering from the won's descent to an all-time low and rising interest rates.
The Capel Korea index was down 1.14 points, or 1.54 percent, at 72.90, a premium of 35.77 percent.

Taiwan GDRs held their ground but also failed to follow the strong lead from Wall Street overnight as the domestic market remained capped by concerns over typhoon damage and a looming cabinet reshuffle.
The Capel Taiwan index was up 0.28 points, or 1.54 percent, at 133.16 -- representing a discount of 5.15 percent.
